response.consequence: The test fails against the current menu. If the count were adjusted to pass, it would not check that the specific items are present or absent.
response.explanation: The beforeEach grants AlertingRuleUpdate and AlertingRuleDelete, in addition to Silence, Create and Read. AlertRuleMenu.tsx renders a Pause item when canPause (update permission), a Delete item when canDelete and a rulerRule exists, and a Divider. Together with Silence, Duplicate, Copy link and Export, that is about 6 menuitems, not 4. The test ignores Pause and Delete, and its own ui.menuItems.delete selector is never asserted. The final `expect(menuItems.length).toBe(4)` therefore contradicts the rendered menu and should fail.
response.title: Menu test asserts exactly 4 items but granted permissions render more

response.consequence: A user with Grafana rule-create permission sees an enabled Duplicate action on non-Grafana (data-source) rules. The ruler-based check would have hidden or disabled it. Support is inferred only from reading the code: the ruler path is not shown, and no caller or test was inspected.
response.explanation: AlertRuleMenu passes skipToken to useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities when promRule isn't a Grafana rule. That makes useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities run with rule === undefined. useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable returns loading: false, so MaybeSupported is AlwaysSupported. The Duplicate ability is then toAbility(AlwaysSupported, rulesPermissions.create) with no check on the rule. AlertRuleMenu combines the two paths with `||`: canDuplicate = ruler || grafana. For a data-source-managed rule, the ruler path may report Duplicate unsupported or not allowed, for example when the ruler is unavailable or the data source is read-only. The skipped Grafana path still reports [true, hasGrafanaCreatePermission]. Duplicate is therefore enabled for rules the Grafana-rule check was meant to skip.
response.title: Skipped Grafana prom-rule ability check still grants Duplicate, OR-ed into AlertRuleMenu

response.consequence: Users with edit or delete permission see these actions enabled for federated (read-only) rules wherever useAllAlertRuleAbilities is the only gate. The backend should reject the actions, but the UI gate has regressed.
response.explanation: useAllAlertRuleAbilities used to compute isFederated with isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group). That made Update, Delete, Pause, Restore and DeletePermanently unsupported for federated rule groups. The change makes it a thin wrapper around useAllRulerRuleAbilities, which hardcodes isFederated = false (a TODO). The CombinedRule's group is no longer consulted, even though the deprecated wrapper still receives it. For a CombinedRule in a federated group, those actions now report as supported, so edit and delete controls show up where they were previously hidden. Other call sites, such as RuleDetailsButtons and RuleViewer, still call isFederatedRuleGroup directly.
response.title: Federated rule group check dropped from useAllAlertRuleAbilities

response.explanation: The change only adds mocks for the plural ability hooks and the singular Grafana hook, plus default neutral mocks in beforeEach. The tests still assert the intended permission behaviors. I did not trace the hooks into the components, so I found no failing input rather than ruling one out by reading the component code.

response.consequence: In the new list view, where rules are passed as `promRule` only, "Silence notifications" appears in the menu but clicking it does nothing.
response.explanation: The change lets RuleActionsButtons be used with only `promRule`. AlertRuleMenu then computes `canSilence` from the Grafana prom-rule ability and shows "Silence notifications". Clicking it calls `setShowSilenceDrawer(true)`. The drawer is only rendered when `rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)` is true, and `rule` is undefined in this case. So the drawer never renders.
